title: What a VPN hides from others, and what it doesn't
description: A VPN changes who can see your traffic, but it doesn't make you anonymous or protect you from malware. Here's the honest version.

scenes.big: A VPN isn't an invisibility cloak
scenes.sub: it moves who can see what
scenes.say: A VPN is not an invisibility cloak. It just changes who can see what.

scenes.sub: log in, and the site knows you
scenes.say: First, the myth. A VPN doesn't make you anonymous. Log in to an account, and the site knows exactly who you are.

lines: Websites see the VPN server's address
Your VPN provider can still see your traffic
scenes.say: What it does change is your address. Websites see the VPN server's address, not your home one. Handy for privacy, but it only covers that one thing.

steps: The VPN server forwards it on
The site sees the server, not you
scenes.say: Your traffic is encrypted on the way to the VPN server, which forwards it. So café Wi-Fi owners and your internet provider can't see what you're doing.
But the VPN company sits in the middle instead, so you're trusting them. And a VPN won't stop malware or phishing. Choose carefully. Follow for more plain truths.
